newsitem.title: USA: Indiana corn one pct harvested vs four pct average.
newsitem.headline: Indiana corn one pct harvested vs four pct average.

text.p: Indiana's corn crop was one percent harvested as of Sunday and 20 percent of the crop was mature, behind the 39 percent average, according to Indiana Agricultural Statistics Service.
Normally, four percent of the acreage would have been harvested as of Sunday. Corn was rated four percent very poor, 15 percent poor, 40 fair, 37 good and four percent excellent.
Sixty-two percent of the crop had reached the dent stage, compared with 92 percent last year and 90 percent for the five-year average.
Soybeans were rated six percent very poor, 16 percent poor, 43 percent fair, 31 percent good and four percent excellent, about the same as the previous week.
Fifteen percent of the soybean acreage was shedding leaves, against 41 percent average.

Rains during the week aided topsoil moisture levels with 19 percent rated very short, compared with 38 percent the previous week. Moisture also was rated 36 percent short, 43 percent adequate and two percent surplus.
Pasture and range condition was rated 14 percent very poor, 30 percent poor, 40 fair, 15 good and one percent excellent.
